A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MFC with lower ESR can be regarded as having better contact states and thus better pulse handling capability in high current densities.
the ESR at low frequencies is an efficient parameter for the quality of contact status between spray and metallization and can be used for evaluating the pulse handling capability of capacitors.
the pulse lifetime is determined by the end contact status, which can be reflected by the ESR at low frequencies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

ESR at high frequency (∼10 MHz) can be used as a parameter to characterize the contact status between the spray and film, while ESR at low frequencies (∼100 kHz) can be used to evaluate the pulse lifetime of MFC.

the pulse handling capability of the metallized film capacitive energy storage can be evaluated through the equivalent series resistance ( ESR ) at low frequencies (100 Hz) rather than at high frequencies (10 kHz).

low frequency ESR is more sensitive to the contact quality between the spray and the metallization, and it is more efficient to evaluate the pulse lifetime and the pulse handling capability of metallized film capacitive.
